title: Plasma closes windows one by one on Wayland during restart -> losing browser tabs
line: Logging out or restarting no longer makes web browsers forget all their windows but the last one.
explanation: On Wayland logout, plasma-shutdown asks KWin (org.kde.KWin.Session.closeWaylandWindows) to close every remaining toplevel, and KWin sent xdg_toplevel.close to each window. Chromium-based browsers and Firefox handle each of those as the user closing that window while others are still open, so they drop it from their saved session and only the last window is restored. KDE apps are not affected because ksmserver has already asked them to quit through session management before this step. Now, for windows whose desktop file is in the WebBrowser category, KWin sends SIGTERM once to the browser process instead of closing its windows one by one; browsers treat that as a whole-app quit and keep every window, as on X11 or GNOME. All other apps still get the normal close request, so unsaved-changes prompts and the 'did not close' notification work as before.

commits.message:
sm: Ask web browsers to quit as a whole when logging out

Closing every window of a browser one by one made it treat all but the
last as closed by the user, so only that one came back after logging in
again. Send the browser SIGTERM instead, which it handles as a full quit.

BUG: 511236

media.caption: Pure master: Chrome had windows A (2 tabs), B and C; after the logout window close and relaunching Chrome, only window C came back
With the fix, same steps: all three windows come back, A with both of its tabs
